chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qasani, who said:
One of our companions informed me that he carried to Abu al-Hasan al-Rida عليه السلام a wealth of great value, but I did not see him pleased by it.
He said: So I became distressed because of that, and I said to myself: I have brought this wealth, yet he has not been pleased by it.
Then he said: O servant, the washbasin and the water. He said: Then he sat upon a chair, gestured with his hand, and said to the servant: Pour the water over me.
He said: Then gold began to flow from between his fingers into the washbasin. Then he turned toward me and said to me: One who is like this does not care for that which you carried to him.

key_terms.أَخْبَرَنِي: informed me; introduces the report being narrated
key_terms.الطَّسْتَ: the washbasin brought for collecting the water
key_terms.ذَهَبٌ: gold, appearing here as a miraculous manifestation
key_terms.لَا يُبَالِي: does not care or attach importance
key_terms.لَهُ خَطَرٌ: of great worth or serious value
key_terms.مَالًا: wealth or property of material value

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith show Imam al-Rida’s عليه السلام lack of concern for worldly wealth?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates an extraordinary sign from Imam al-Rida عليه السلام when a man brought him a large amount of wealth and felt troubled at seeing no sign of pleasure. The Imam demonstrated that material wealth held no significance for him by causing gold to flow from between his fingers, showing his detachment from worldly riches and manifesting a miraculous sign.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Muhammad, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ali Bin Muhammad Al Qasany who said,
‘One of our companions informed me that he carried over a lot of wealth to Abu Al-Hassan Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup>, but did not see any happiness with him<sup>asws</sup>.
He said, ‘So I was gloomy due to that and I said within myself, ‘I have carried (all) this wealth and he<sup>asws</sup> is not happy with it?’
So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘O boy! The washbasin and the water!’ So he<sup>asws</sup> sat upon a chair and gestured by his<sup>asws</sup> hand and said to the boy: ‘Pour the water upon me’.

So gold flowed from in front of his<sup>asws</sup> fingers in the washbasin. Then he<sup>asws</sup> turned towards me and he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘The one who was like this does not care of that which is carried over to him’.
en.sarwar: 9. al-Husayn ibnmmd has narrated from Mu‘alla ibnmd from Musafir and from al-Washsha’ from Musafir who has said the following.

“When Harun ibn al-Musayyib decided to fight Muhammad ibn Ja‘far, abu al-Hassan (a.s.) told me to go to him and say, “Do not go our tomorrow. If would do so you will be defeated and your people will be killed.”

If he would ask, “How do youknow that?” Say, “I saw it in my dream.” The narrator has said that he went to him and said, “May Allah make of service to you, do not go out tomorrow to fight. If would do so you will be defeated and your people will be killed.”

He asked, “How do you know this?” I said, “I saw it in my dream.” He said, “A slave goes to sleep (to dream) and his behind is not even washed.” He went out to fight. He was defeated and his people were killed.” The narrator has said that Musafir narrated, “I was in the presenceof al-Rida (a.s.) in Mina, Makka that Yahya ibn Khalid passed by and he covered his head from the dust. The Imam (a.s.) said, “Poor people do not know what will happen to them this year.”
I, by Allah, could not understand themeaning of his statement until we buried him (Yahya ibn Khalid).”
